title: Responsibility, risk and jazz records that sell forever
summary: Carter wishes someone shared the decision and notes jazz records sell slowly but forever.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Because I just wonder ... you know, about that, that is, if they quote, a "serious" musician sits down, a lot of things that are specified for the commercial musician, how long it is, how many instruments, are all compositional decisions, that this "serious" musician has to make for himself. For the commercial musicians, these decisions have been made for him, in effect.
Well, in this particular instance, I
I have to make this decision for myself, and as much as I wanted it, I would really like to have some direction, you know?

I guess maybe I want someone to share the responsibility. You know, maybe that's it, because I said to Norman, I said, I know that jazz records don't sell a million to begin with -- maybe with some exceptions; I understand that George Benson has a big exception right of as of this moment -- but I would like to think if you're going to invest a lot of money in an album, I would like to hope that -- because jazz records don't sell a lot instantly, but they do sell forever.

You know? I'd like to feel that at least, in your lifetime, if not in mine, you'll be able to recover your investment. You know. So he laughed and he wasn't too worried about that. He's not too profit motivated. He does so many things for his own pleasure. So I'm going ahead and get started on this in the next few days.
Well, what kind of things are going through your mind now, as you do this? He says, go ahead and do what you want.
